claims.text: High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering will improve the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite relative to an untreated composite.
The treatment will produce a 20% improvement in thermal conductivity.
High-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering will produce a more homogeneous distribution of W and Cu phases.
High-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering will enhance interfacial contact between W and Cu.
High-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering will reduce interfacial voids.
Mechanical alloying during ball milling breaks down the W and Cu phases.
Ball milling creates fresh W and Cu surfaces.
Fresh surfaces created by ball milling facilitate W-Cu interdiffusion during spark plasma sintering.
Fresh surfaces created by ball milling facilitate W-Cu interfacial bonding during spark plasma sintering.
Interdiffusion and bonding during spark plasma sintering reduce W-Cu phase separation.
Improved phase homogeneity, interfacial contact, and reduced void content cause higher thermal conductivity.
The proposed process uses ball milling at 200 rpm for 5 hours.
The proposed spark plasma sintering step uses 800°C for 30 minutes under 50 MPa.
The predicted improvement applies under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components.
The magnitude of the conductivity improvement may depend on the specific ball-milling and spark-plasma-sintering conditions.
The magnitude of the conductivity improvement may depend on the irradiation stability of the W-Cu composite.
